newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Parana to invest 26 mln reais in cotton.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Parana to invest 26 mln reais in cotton.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Parana will invest 26 million reais ($24 million) in its flagging cotton sector this year to prevent planting from hitting a record low in 1997/98, the state agricultural secretariat said.

"The state government's target for the next harvest is to plant 250,000 hectares," the secretariat said in a statement. "The government is going to invest, through subsidies, close to 26 million reais."
Parana growers planted 59,700 hectares of cotton in 1996/97, harvesting 36,000 tonnes, one of its lowest crops in history.

"Each producer who plants up to six hectares of cotton (this harvest) will receive calcium, seeds and the use of machines to prepare the soil," State Agricultural Secretary Hermas Brandao was quoted as saying.
The state government hopes its program will create 150,000 new jobs.
Planting of the 1997/98 harvest was due to begin on September 15 and last until October 20, according to Parana cooperatives association Ocepar, which forecasts 130,000 hectares will be planted.
